articles.title: Analysis: Jensen’s homecoming puts Nvidia under a sharper spotlight
articles.short_snippet: Jensen Huang is back at the helm of Nvidia—the designer of highly advanced AI chips, the world's most valuable company, and a key player underpinning hundreds of billions of US dollars' worth of AI-related financing. Yet with several investigations ongoing and national security concerns unresolved, the story is not over.

articles.title: TSMC eyes US$22.6 billion Texas campus for 2nm chips
articles.short_snippet: TSMC is considering a US$22.6 billion semiconductor manufacturing campus in Texas, including about US$14 billion in machinery and equipment investment, as the chipmaker weighs Texas against Arizona for its next major US expansion.

articles.title: Samsung memory capacity through 2029 largely under contract, Korean report says
articles.short_snippet: AI data center demand is pushing memory supply negotiations years into the future. Most of Samsung Electronics' memory chip production capacity for 2027 through 2029 is already secured under contract, South Korean outlet Economy Tribune reported on November 21, citing a person familiar with the matter. Samsung has not publicly confirmed the report.

articles.title: ADATA secures US$9.12 billion sustainability-linked loan
articles.short_snippet: ADATA Technology completed a NT$300 billion (US$9.12 billion) sustainability-linked syndicated loan on November 24, securing commitments from nine financial institutions and exceeding its original fundraising target. The financing was arranged to repay existing bank borrowings and provide medium-term working capital as the Taiwan-based memory module maker expands its operations.

articles.title: Analysis: Six million orders on the line – China's Nvidia supply gap persists despite Huang's return
articles.short_snippet: Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO on November 23 has restored confidence in the global AI computing market, but Chinese cloud providers face a more fundamental challenge: securing sufficient computing capacity under increasingly restrictive US export controls.

articles.title: Z.ai unveils GLM-5.4, debuting loop transformer architecture, general coding paradigm
articles.short_snippet: Chinese artificial intelligence firm Z.ai officially released its next-generation flagship model, GLM-5.4, marking the company's first flagship model built on a loop transformer architecture and the starting point of its push toward a general coding paradigm.

articles.title: US blacklists Megaspeed amid Nvidia chip smuggling probe; Alibaba disputes affiliate listing
articles.short_snippet: The US Department of Commerce added Singapore-based cloud firm Megaspeed and six of its Southeast Asian affiliates to its trade blacklist on Monday, escalating a federal crackdown on alleged artificial intelligence chip smuggling to China amid intense scrutiny from lawmakers and administration officials.

articles.title: Taiwan stocks soar over 9% as Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia sparks global market rally
articles.short_snippet: Global equities staged a dramatic recovery following the surprise return of Jensen Huang as chief executive officer of Nvidia, reigniting investor confidence in the artificial intelligence sector and sparking a massive relief rally across Wall Street and Asia.

articles.title: Huawei's HarmonyOS crosses 100 million devices, taking on Apple beyond smartphones
articles.short_snippet: Huawei officially announced on November 24 that the number of devices running native HarmonyOS had surpassed 100 million, marking a milestone in the Chinese technology giant's efforts to establish an independent operating system (OS) ecosystem spanning smartphones, PCs, wearables and vehicles.

articles.title: Infineon adapts automotive and industrial chip technologies to advance the development of humanoid robots
articles.short_snippet: Infineon Technologies is adapting its automotive and industrial semiconductor technologies for humanoid robots, with functional safety, dexterity and power efficiency emerging as key development priorities. However, a timeline for significant production will develop with market needs.

articles.title: Amazon to acquire Decart optimization technology and bring team aboard
articles.short_snippet: Amazon's purchase of Decart's technology and recruitment of its founders and research team could strengthen the company's efforts to improve AI inference speed and computing efficiency worldwide. The transaction would connect Decart's full-stack optimization expertise with Amazon's custom silicon portfolio, although completion remains subject to conditions, including regulatory clearance.

articles.title: Analysis: Samsung, SK Hynix look beyond Nvidia as Huang returns
articles.short_snippet: Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO has eased concerns among South Korean memory chipmakers over high-bandwidth memory (HBM) supply agreements and next-generation chip development, but growing demand for AI processors from Google, Amazon, and other technology companies continues to reshape the memory market.

articles.title: Commentary: Lens' semiconductor strategy offers Apple's Chinese suppliers a path up the value chain
articles.short_snippet: Lens Technology founder Zhou Qunfei is expanding her semiconductor investment strategy from direct stakes in chip companies to broader industry participation, offering a model for how Apple's Chinese suppliers can diversify beyond consumer electronics without abandoning their manufacturing strengths.

articles.title: Micron steps up HBM investment in Taiwan, Singapore
articles.short_snippet: Micron Technology is stepping up investment in high-bandwidth memory (HBM) production in Taiwan and Singapore as it seeks to narrow the capacity gap with South Korean rivals Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.

articles.title: Analysis: Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia, but he is returning to a changed board
articles.short_snippet: Nvidia's board took six days to go from ruling out Jensen Huang's return to reinstating him. Despite that, its own filings show the founder will be coming back to a different company. Nvidia now has its first board chair, an ongoing investigation, and a new layer of national security oversight. All three took shape while Huang was gone.

articles.title: IPC makers see no AI project delays after US midterms as edge server inquiries rise
articles.short_snippet: Several industrial PC (IPC) makers said their AI-related projects are proceeding as planned, with no clear delays so far, even as the market reassesses the returns on heavy AI spending by cloud service providers (CSPs) amid uncertainty over US energy and AI policy following the midterm elections. Some said customer inquiries for edge servers have increased.

articles.title: Sarvam's foreign-model platform tests India's AI-sovereignty goals
articles.short_snippet: Sarvam's decision to host Chinese-developed AI models on Indian infrastructure is putting a practical question at the center of India's push for technological independence: whether sovereignty depends on owning the models, controlling the computing infrastructure, or both.

articles.title: Rene Haas, once touted as possible Nvidia successor, commits to lead Arm to 2033
articles.short_snippet: Arm CEO Rene Haas has confirmed that he will extend his leadership of the company under a new agreement lasting until 2033. Previously, he had been considered a top contender to lead Nvidia after the resignation of Jensen Huang, who has since been reinstated as CEO.

articles.short_snippet: Samsung Electronics plans to boost production capacity for its ninth-generation (V9) NAND flash memory fivefold at its second plant in Xi'an, China, by November 2027 to meet demand for enterprise solid-state drives (eSSDs) used in AI data centers, Seoul Economic Daily reported, citing industry sources.

articles.title: Ukraine defense tech firm Uforce raises US$700 million, eyes Asia-Pacific production, Taiwan suppliers

The funding will be used to help the company expand research and development of its unmanned systems, as well as support efforts to move production facilities closer to frontline markets.

articles.title: Cisco, OpenAI launch open-source project to counter AI-driven cyberattacks
articles.short_snippet: Cisco Systems and OpenAI have launched an open-source cybersecurity project designed to protect running Linux systems from attacks while permanent software patches are being developed.

articles.title: Macronix bets on 3D NAND and NOR as bigger rivals retreat from low-capacity markets
articles.short_snippet: Macronix International is betting on 3D NAND and 3D NOR flash memory to drive its next phase of growth as major global memory manufacturers withdraw from low- and mid-capacity markets, leaving opportunities in automotive and other specialty applications.

articles.title: Zenitron sees little relief for DRAM shortages even with new memory capacity in 2H27
articles.short_snippet: IC distributor Zenitron expects new memory production capacity to come online in the second half of 2027, easing overall supply. Still, memory prices are unlikely to collapse even if they correct, while DRAM remains very tight, co-CEO Andrew Chou said.

articles.title: SpaceX prices US$44 billion Nvidia chip financing, with most debt yielding above 8%
articles.short_snippet: SpaceX has priced about US$44 billion in financing tied to Nvidia chips, with most of the roughly US$32 billion in debt notes yielding more than 8%—well above typical investment-grade levels and a sign that investors remain wary of whether heavy AI spending will pay off, according to Bloomberg and Quartz .

articles.short_snippet: Competition in the US commercial space launch market is intensifying as Stoke Space, a rocket startup founded just seven years ago, seeks to challenge SpaceX with technology designed to make an entire launch vehicle reusable.
